articles.title_original: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit
articles.title_zh: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit
facts_zh:
EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit
- Published
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has laid out her vision for what an "associate membership" status for Canada to the EU would look like as officials gather in Montreal to discuss closer ties.
It is "a partnership that comes close to membership than anything we have done before," she said on Thursday's remarks at the two-day Canada-EU summit.

She added it is a type of relationship that would be open "only to our closest partners outside of Europe who are ready to open a new frontier together."
It includes close alignment on governance and policies, and partnering in research and innovation.

all_titles.en: EU chief lays out vision for new Canada partnership at Montreal summit

articles.title_original: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
facts_zh:
Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show
- Published
Partial results from Israel's general election show veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu marginally ahead of his rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, but still short of a majority in parliament.
With 99% of ballots counted, Netanyahu's Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies were on track to win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
Eisenkot's Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc were set for 48.

all_titles.en: Netanyahu's bloc leading Israel election but short of majority, partial results show

articles.title_original: Nvidia CEO reportedly targeted by Chinese spy
articles.title_zh: Nvidia CEO reportedly targeted by Chinese spy
facts_zh: Jensen Huang reported to have had close relationship with tech company executive suspected of passing intel to China US intelligence agencies believe the Nvidia chief executive, Jensen Huang, has been targeted by a Chinese spy who had done business with him, according to a new report by the New York Times.
Alice Huang or Huang Le, of no relation to the Nvidia CEO, is an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed.
She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China , prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her.

articles.title_original: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say
articles.title_zh: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say
facts_zh:
Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say
- Published
At least 14 people have been killed after a Russian jet-powered drone hit a crowded platform at the main railway station in the central Ukrainian city of Dnipro, local officials have said.
Dnipropetrovsk regional head Oleksandr Hanzha said at least 14 others were wounded in the attack, including an 11-year-old boy.
Ukraine's state railway operator, Ukrzaliznytsia, said a passenger train headed for the southern city of Zaporizhzhia was at one of the platforms in Dnipro when the drone hit.

all_titles.en: Russian drone attack on Ukrainian train station kills at least 14, officials say

articles.title_original: Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports
articles.title_zh: Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports
facts_zh:
Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports
- Published
At least two people have been killed and five injured after a rock formation collapsed at a tourist site in Turkey's historical region of Cappadocia, local media is reporting.
One of the rock spires, which are known as fairy chimneys, reportedly disintegrated at the popular open-air museum in the central town of Göreme.
Nevşehir provincial Governor Hüseyin Kök said the victims' bodies had been recovered from under the rubble, but the justice minister warned there could be "other potential victims" still trapped.

all_titles.en: Rock collapse kills two in Turkey's Cappadocia, local media reports

articles.title_zh: Record number of purges as Xi emphasises 'party discipline' at China political gathering
facts_zh:
Record number of purges as Xi emphasises 'party discipline' at China political gathering
- Published
A record 33 members have been expelled from China's Communist Party as it concluded a major annual political gathering, which had the most empty seats ever seen.
The fifth plenum was attended by 279 Central Committee members, compared to 315 at the fourth plenum in October 2025 and 364 at the third one in July 2024.
While recent plenums focused on economic reforms or social and development issues, party discipline took centre stage at this week's gathering.

all_titles.en: Record number of purges as Xi emphasises 'party discipline' at China political gathering

articles.title_zh: US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry over DR Congo conflict
facts_zh:
US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry over DR Congo conflict
- Published
The United States has imposed sanctions on Rwanda's defence ministry over its alleged support for the M23 rebel group in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, increasing pressure on Kigali to withdraw its troops and halt support for the rebels.
"Rwanda must halt its support for M23 and withdraw its troops from eastern DRC," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said.
The sanctions come months after Rwanda and DR Congo signed a US-brokered peace agreement aimed at ending the conflict.

all_titles.en: US sanctions Rwanda's defence ministry over DR Congo conflict

articles.title_original: Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
articles.title_zh: Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
facts_zh:
Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
- Published
Audio recordings published in Spanish media reveal conversations between train drivers and a railway control centre in the minutes leading up to a deadly train crash that killed at least 69 people and injured dozens.
Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train on Wednesday morning.

Three audio recordings between the control centre in Madrid and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another some 25km (15 miles) up ahead had stalled.

all_titles.en: Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash

articles.title_zh: Audacious Indian jailbreak saga ends with 17 prisoners recaptured
facts_zh:
Audacious Indian jailbreak saga ends with 17 prisoners recaptured
- Published
A fake medical emergency, an audacious jailbreak and a 36-hour search operation that ended with 17 prisoners being recaptured.
Those are the highlights of a story from India's Tamil Nadu state that has captured headlines across the country.
It began on Monday night after 17 men escaped from a prison in Theni district in the southern state after overpowering guards, and ended almost two days later with police catching them in batches.

all_titles.en: Audacious Indian jailbreak saga ends with 17 prisoners recaptured

Ethiopia acquires Russian fighter jets and air defence systems amid war in Tigray
- Published
Ethiopia has received 12 Su-35 fighter jets from Russia, as fighting intensified in the northern Tigray region neighbouring Eritrea.
Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, who is attending the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow, described the acquisition as a "milestone" that would boost Ethiopia's defence capacity.
He said Ethiopia and Russia had agreed on the deal several years ago and the warplanes had come ahead of schedule.

facts_zh:
El Salvador sends 2,000 troops to Haiti to rescue four missing soldiers
- Published
El Salvador has deployed more than 2,000 soldiers to Haiti as part of a mission to retrieve four nationals who went missing in the Caribbean country almost two weeks ago.

The "robust deployment" was communicated by El Salvador President Nayib Bukele to the Prime Minister of Haiti Alix Didier Fils-Aime earlier this week, the foreign ministry of El Salvador said in a statement on Wednesday.
Bukele said the soldiers would also assist ongoing "security efforts against gangs in Haiti", the statement continued.
